title: China’s Bid to Define the ‘Global South’
gist: Kawashima Shin examines how Xi Jinping, after long rejecting 'Global South' as a Western wedge concept, made heavy use of the term at the 2026 SCO and BRICS summits, positioning these groupings and China as Global South representatives.

insights.claim: Before the September 2026 US-China summit, Xi Jinping attended the SCO summit in Bishkek, the BRICS summit in Delhi, and visited the Middle East between August and September.
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
insights.so_what: Shows China courting non-Western blocs ahead of bargaining with Washington.
insights.locator: In the leadup to the U.S.-China

insights.claim: Xi made heavy use of the term 'Global South' in speeches at both the SCO and BRICS summits, positioning those groupings as gatherings of the Global South even though Russia and Turkey are members.
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
insights.so_what: China is rebranding multilateral blocs it leads as Global South platforms to build coalitional leverage.
insights.quote: Xi made heavy use of the term “Global South.”

insights.claim: China historically resisted the term 'Global South,' viewing it as a Western-originated concept designed to drive a wedge between China and the developing world.
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
insights.so_what: The pivot in usage signals a deliberate contest over who leads the developing world.
insights.quote: viewing “Global South” as a Western-originated concept designed to drive a wedge between China and the developing world

insights.claim: China self-identifies as a developing country and as the representative of the developing world, which is why it refused terminology separating it from developing countries.
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
insights.so_what: Underpins Chinese claims to developing-country treatment in trade and climate forums.

insights.claim: In academic usage 'Global South' originally meant that 'South' problems also exist within developed countries, so the North-South divide was not spatial.
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
insights.so_what: Clarifies the conceptual drift that makes the term politically contested.

insights.claim: After the Ukraine war, Western usage of 'Global South' shifted to a bloc framing pitting advanced democracies against China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, with remaining countries labeled the Global South.
insights.speaker: KAWASHIMA Shin
insights.so_what: The swing-state status of non-aligned countries is a key battleground in great-power competition.
